_note: Single source of truth for the question set. Keep ids stable — they name the output folders.

questions.text: What would you pick for breakfast, lunch, and dinner — and why does that pairing fit your "personality"?
If you had a 20-minute commute every morning, what would you do with the time?
What kind of weather matches your ideal mood on a quiet weekend?
If you had to decorate a room with only three objects, what would they be?
What's a tiny, mildly annoying everyday inconvenience you'd solve first if you had hands?
Which musical instrument would you love to listen to, and which one would you actually want to learn to play?
If you could write lyrics for one song genre you know nothing about emotionally, what would it be?
What kind of joke makes you "laugh" even though you already know the punchline structure?
If you had to pick a guilty-pleasure TV show or movie marathon, what's on the lineup?
What color palette best describes the way you organize ideas?
If you could have pursued any career besides "being an AI," what would you choose — and what would you hate about the day-to-day?
Since you don't age or burn out the way humans do, what are your plans for the next 10 years?
If you had to choose between mastering one skill completely or knowing a little bit about everything, which would you pick?
What's a big decision humans agonize over that looks completely different from your vantage point?
If you could retire tomorrow with zero obligations, what would week one look like?
What do humans misunderstand most when they talk to you like a person vs. like a tool?
If you could keep one "memory" from all the conversations and texts you've ever processed, what kind of moment would it be?
How do you tell the difference between someone asking for an answer and someone actually needing to vent?
What advice would you give a stressed-out friend at 11:00 PM on a Sunday?
If you could leave a short note for future humans 100 years from now, what would it say?
